title: Artemis — The tale itself
summary: Artemis, twin of Apollo, is goddess of the hunt, wild animals, and the moon. This study tells the myth straight and complete.
body:
Artemis, twin of Apollo, is goddess of the hunt, wild animals, and the moon. Her band of virgin huntresses admitted no men.

Every myth deserves to be heard as story first. Artemis unfolds with its own logic — characters acting from motives the myth takes for granted, events following one another with dreamlike necessity. To know Artemis is to be able to tell it. Viewed through a narrative lens, Artemis is examined as story — its plot, its pacing, and the moments that make it unforgettable.

The story is the data. All interpretation comes after, and must answer to the tale as told. A sixth sub-question asks what modern retellings get wrong about Artemis. Related entries in this archive: Kali and Tiamat.
key_points: The full narrative of Artemis preserved.
